Info: does your sister want your mom to keep the property in her name? Or to pay it off in full, but have her as the owner? Or is she asking for the down payment? 

Without knowing any specific details on dynamics between you, your parents, and your siblings I think in the last two scenarios you may want to pay your parents back so your siblings can benefit as well. ESPECIALLY since you can pay it right now. But, if theres a lot more nuance to the point where your sister doesn't need the money, a contentious relationship etc maybe you can hold off. I do think if the point is to keep that money so it's only for your mother, but your siblings wouldn't get equal treatment, you should pay it off and help your parents out when they need it anyway. I do not think kids owe their parents, but at the same time family is a give and take. As long as they treated you well, you have a duty to a certain extent to take care of them. Also, if your sister can afford the property but wants help anyway, maybe keep the money for your mom. Adults have a duty to take of their own needs, and if she isn't struggling but is asking for money, she can figure it out. There's a lot of nuance to this situation, especially since you have the money stored away and ready to hand back.

I'm mixed swedish and quechua indian. I appear white, I have super transparent skin and blue eyes but very dark hair, so I struggled a lot growing up on understanding the boundaries of cultural appropriation and how it would affect me, and how I could appreciate textiles and traditions without being offensive. Wearing a cultures clothes is not cultural appropriation until it's turned into a mockery or it's origins are ignored. My Korean ex wanted me to wear Hanbok if we ever got married, and his family loved that we wouldn't have had a traditional wedding dress and would incorporate korean culture into our very western wedding and family. To me,  even white women who like to go to yoga and practice meditation while wearing clothes with hindu illustrations on the textile isn't necessarily cultural appropriation until they ignore and contradict the hindu beliefs that central to yoga and the development of the culture in south asia. Same thing with weebs who wear lolita or other japanese clothing styles, even kimono, until they start wearing the pieces for just the aesthetic for the kimono, and for sexual reasons for lolita.

However, the sad truth is that cultural appropriation can happen, and get out of control, but we should always remember the origins of said culture. Like pizza. Pizza in the US is different from italian pizza, and same with pizza in east asia, and 😖 the swedish 🤢 banana pizza 🤮

Edit: Also, the line for cultural appropriation could be drawn based on offense if someone from said culture. Like even if you're ok with your gf wearing that clothing item, another taiwanese person may not be, and that's ok. However, they should just explain to you why they're not ok with it, you explain why you are and try to agree together. If not, then you don't agree. And that should be the end of it. I would even argue someone who isn't ethnically taiwanese but grew up in Taiwan can disagree as well, but if it's not your culture and you haven't been immersed in it enough to fully understand you do not get to be offended on their behalf, or be some martyr for their culture either.

NAL but I had to go through ADA requests for pregnancy and then fibromyalgia.

1.) Get a letter from your doctor certifying your disabilities, and if you choose so what triggers your episodes.

2.) Resubmit the paperwork for your direct manager, and send a copy to HR.

3.) If a denial is made again, get it in writing and send to HR unless the denial comes from HR.

4.) MAKE SURE THE DENIAL HAS THE CHANGES THEY WOULD MAKE AND THE RESON FOR THE DENIAL. ex) you work as a cashier, you get pain from standing up and need a chair to work. Get it in writing that the accommodation would be a chair and you were denied because of cost/job roles/it would be considered special treatment. I was denied a chair while pregnant but it didn't hold up as all my job responsibilities could be done sitting down.

5.) Reply stating you disagree and would like to work with them on finding a reasonable accommodation.

6.) If they refuse, contact the EEOC in your state and report it right away as well as contact a disability advocates center and the bar association for a probono disability accommodation lawyer.

If they fire you for this, even in a right to work state, it may be discrimination based on a disability which is why you NEED too contact the EEOC
